# Infernal cmalign native fixtures

`native/*/{alignment.sto,scores.txt,inserts.txt,local_ends.txt}` are byte copies
of actual Infernal 1.1.5 runs. `metadata.json` is caller-supplied metadata copied
or extracted from the retained input files and actual invocation arguments.
No scientific result bytes were generated by a mock or rewritten as fixtures.

The `interleaved_stress` and `pfam_stress` cases use an explicitly artificial
input: the tutorial Cobalamin sequence with 32 U symbols inserted after position
61. Their outputs are real native executions used to exceed Stockholm's
200-column wrapping boundary and compare actual Stockholm/Pfam serialization.
This sequence is not presented as an observed biological molecule. Its exact
transformation and hash are retained in the native receipt.

Original model/sequence sources are the installed Infernal 1.1.5 tutorial files.
Mutable copies, exact commands, stdout/stderr, input/binary hashes, resource
limits and native failure receipts are retained in
`verification/tool_graders_infernal_alignment_2026-10-26_220/`.
`NATIVE_SHA256.json` independently checks fixture bytes against those copies.

The training model itself was made by Infernal 1.1.4 (its native header records
that fact); alignment execution used the installed 1.1.5 binary. No model
header was relabeled. Local-end Cobalamin input is the tutorial's selected
RNA sequence. These fixtures verify program formats/calculations; they do not
establish experimentally observed structure or gene function.

Synthetic adversarial Stockholm and sidecar strings are constructed explicitly
inside `tests/test_cmalign_graders.py`. They are kept separate from this native
fixture directory and are not described as executed scientific measurements.
